Clothoid cut

The eye is (√π/2, √π/2). Cut the curve at the origin and box one half: the box's best width is a double normal, not a double tangent. The full ± curve on a table is a different pair — 38.5° clockwise leaves its outer turns level to 0.00002.

The centre is exact. With x(s)=∫cos(t²/2)dt and u=s/√2, the limit is √2∫₀^∞cos(u²)du = √π/2, so the two eyes are (±√π/2, ±√π/2) = (±0.886227, ±0.886227). The line joining them is y=x and it passes through the origin. The equal-arc cut is at the origin; the spiral crosses that line infinitely often on the way to the eye, and those later crossings are windings, not cuts.

The box minimum is measured, not a guess. For a direction n the width is max(p·n) − min(p·n). Scanning the convex hull and refining gives the numbers below. At a minimum the two support lines are parallel and each is tangent at one point — a double normal. The box edge is the tangent line, so the two tangent lines are distinct whenever the width is positive. A double tangent needs one line touching twice, which the box cannot supply.

curvemin widthangleheight at that angle
half, s ≥ 00.8977150.5°1.6161
full, s ≥ 0 plus its point reflection0.9838128.5°3.3598

The 0.079 figure is the same-half mirror join, where both contacts are on one half (the table on hearts.html); that pair sits near the eye. The full ± curve is different: at 38.5° clockwise its two outer turns are level to 0.00002 (Fig. 5). That is the usable table contact. The box's best is still 0.984, so the box is not that join.

Fig. 1 · the cut

the two halves are point reflections; the cut is at the origin on the line between the eyes

Fig. 2 · one half, minimum width

the two blue edges are the support lines and the tangent lines; they are parallel and 0.898 apart, not the same line

The full pair

Boxing both halves together does not help. The minimum width is 0.9838, and the two support points are point reflections of each other; the two tangent lines are again distinct.

Fig. 3 · both halves, minimum width

full min width 0.9838 at 128.5° · height 3.3598

Width against rotation

The ink curve is the half; the blue curve is the full pair. The dots are the minima. The width function is periodic in 180°, and neither minimum is zero.

Fig. 4 · width vs angle

half 0.8977 at 150.5° · full 0.9838 at 128.5°

The table contact

Rotate the whole ± curve by 38.5° clockwise and the two outer-turn points are level to 0.00002 units — visually a table contact, not exactly. The two points are on the outer turns, not near the eye, so this is a heart-sized pair. It is a different object from the same-half mirror join (0.079) and from the minimum-width box (0.984): here one support line touches twice.
